item.title: 13-year-old carves 500-pound monster pumpkin, planted with seeds from his grandmother
item.description: When a 13-year-old got the gift of pumpkin seeds from his grandmother, he chose not to toss them aside, but to plant them and be patient. With the help of a forklift, a saw, and a chisel, he carved the 500-pound monster and its little 300-pound sibling. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: Inside the hourslong search for missing boy in Maryland: "I got him!"
item.description: Police found a little boy just feet from a busy road, with the help of a bloodhound named Bo. Tom Hanson has the story.

item.title: Tropical Storm Isaias forms in Gulf, could reach U.S. as hurricane this weekend
item.description: Tropical Storm Isaias has formed in the Gulf and is expected to become a hurricane by Thursday before approaching the U.S. northern Gulf Coast on Friday, according to forecasters.

item.title: Looking back 3 years after Oct. 7, 2023: "There was the constant fear"
item.description: Wednesday marks three years since Hamas terrorists killed more than 1,200 Israelis, including dozens of Americans, and took 250 people hostage. Holly Williams reports from Tel Aviv.

item.title: Christa Pike has pneumonia, unable to move arms after botched execution
item.description: Attorneys for Christa Pike, the Tennessee inmate who survived two doses of a lethal injection during her botched execution last week, shared an update on her health condition.

item.title: Man eyed Mall of America for attack, pledged allegiance to ISIS, FBI says
item.description: An 18-year-old Twin Cities man accused of telling an FBI informant he planned to carry out an attack later this month at Mall of America was arrested at gunpoint Tuesday in Richfield, Minnesota, during an arranged meeting to buy an assault rifle, according to a federal criminal complaint filed Wednesday.

item.title: Exclusive videos show Iranian drone strike on U.S. base in Kuwait
item.description: Video shows an Iranian drone strike on a U.S. military installation in Kuwait, one of at least eight different countries to face Iranian fire in this war, which has damaged or destroyed billions in U.S. military property. Jonah Kaplan has the exclusive.

item.title: What Christa Pike asked when she woke up from failed execution
item.description: Christa Pike's attorneys accuse Tennessee prison officials of delaying access to their client for over two hours after she regained consciousness on Tuesday following a failed execution attempt. Skyler Henry has more.

item.title: WHO questions Russia: "If plague is ruled out, what did she actually die from?"
item.description: The World Health Organization is demanding answers from Russia amid reports of a second suspected case of plague. Imtiaz Tyab reports.

item.title: Jane Doe in Cornell case facing multiple threats, attorney says
item.description: The woman at the center of an alleged gang rape at Cornell University has been facing threats to her family home, according to her attorney. Lilia Luciano reports from Ithaca, New York.

item.title: How FBI foiled ISIS-inspired plot at Mall of America in Minnesota
item.description: Authorities say 18-year-old Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud planned to carry out an ISIS-inspired shooting at the Mall of America in Minnesota. Nicole Sganga reports.

item.title: Tropical Storm Isaias intensifies as shoppers stockpile water, food, essentials
item.description: Warnings of a hurricane threat are posted from Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle. Although the system is a tropical storm, it's expected to strengthen into a Category 2 hurricane by Friday. It would be the first hurricane of the year. Rob Marciano reports from Florida.

item.title: Expert breaks down drug usage on college campuses amid Cornell rape investigation
item.description: Bernadine Waller, assistant professor at Columbia Psychiatry, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss the harm done by drug use on college campuses amid the Cornell University rape investigation.

item.title: Request to halt Texas execution denied in wake of Pike's botched lethal injection
item.description: A Texas court on Wednesday refused to halt the execution of a man who fatally shot a convenience store clerk, after his attorneys cited the failed lethal injection of Christa Pike​ in Tennessee.

item.title: Flu cases rising faster than any recent season, doctor says
item.description: Flu season is off to an early start, with rates highest on the West Coast. CBS News medical correspondent Dr. Céline Gounder shares her insights.

item.title: Michigan GOP Senate candidate Mike Rogers calls for end of Canada tariff war
item.description: Republican Michigan Senate candidate Mike Rogers broke with President Trump in a new campaign ad, saying Canada is not our enemy and that the tariff war needs to end. Former Republican Rep. Fred Upton of Michigan and Democratic strategist Kendra Barkoff Lamy join with analysis.

item.title: Never-before-seen footage shows Iranian attack on U.S. base in Kuwait amid war
item.description: A new video shot from the perspective of a U.S. service member shows an Iranian strike on an American base in Kuwait in the early days of the war. CBS News' Jonah Kaplan reports.

item.title: Democrats' momentum to take Senate growing on Kalshi
item.description: There's talk of an "expanding map" for Democrats, with states like Texas and even Kansas potentially in play for the November midterms. That's reflected in polling and on prediction markets like Kalshi, a CBS News sponsor. Kalshi head of research Nicole Kagan and CBS News executive director of elections and surveys Anthony Salvanto join to unpack the numbers.

item.title: Why Trump is worried about Texas as he makes third trip to state before midterms
item.description: President Trump made a third trip to Texas to campaign for Republican Ken Paxton, who is facing a tight race for Senate with midterms 27 days away. CBS News' Caitlin Huey-Burns shares more details.

item.title: Attorney for accused Cornell fraternity member: "The 7 have been lumped together"
item.description: An attorney for one of the men named in the Cornell rape investigation told CBS News the public has only seen "snippets" of the story and that "the seven have been lumped together." CBS News' Lilia Luciano has more.

item.title: Sen. Thom Tillis says Hegseth is "just out of his depth"
item.description: Republican Sen. Thom Tillis of North Carolina was under intense pressure to confirm Pete Hegseth as defense secretary, and after wavering, he ultimately voted yes. In his new book "How to Lose Friends and Antagonize Presidents," Tillis says that decision hasn't aged well. Tillis joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Vance appears to soften U.S. demands on Iranian nuclear enrichment
item.description: Vance says Iran must do "something meaningful on enrichment capacity" to end the war, as Rubio claims Tehran has "lost complete control" of the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Vance says Iran must reduce nuclear enrichment after originally demanding end to program
item.description: In an interview with Reuters this week, Vice President JD Vance called on Iran to significantly reduce its stockpiles of enriched uranium. Previously, the administration demanded that Tehran end the program. Former Trump national security adviser H. R. McMaster joins "The Takeout" with analysis.

item.title: New videos show Iranian attacks on U.S. military base during early days of war
item.description: CBS News has exclusively obtained video of the Iranian drone strikes and their aftermath at a U.S. military base in northwest Kuwait. Jonah Kaplan has the details.

item.title: Susan Collins and Troy Jackson clash in Maine Senate debate
item.description: Republican Sen. Susan Collins and Maine Democratic Senate candidate Troy Jackson faced off in a debate on Tuesday night. Alex Seitz-Wald, deputy editor of Maine's Midcoast Villager, joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Hegseth presents USS Abraham Lincoln troops with highest honor a military unit can receive
item.description: After more than 300 days at sea, the sailors aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier are about to arrive home in San Diego. They're expected to be back on U.S. soil on Thursday, but Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth flew over a day early to greet the Lincoln's troops and present them with a Presidential Unit Citation. CBS News senior national security correspondent Charlie D'Agata reports.

item.title: FBI concerned alleged Chinese agent is serious flight risk, sources say
item.description: California realtor Wanying Zhang is facing federal prosecution for allegedly surveilling the Taiwanese president's son in Washington last year at the direction of Chinese government officials.

item.title: Maduro expected to face new charges of torture of Americans in Venezuelan prisons
item.description: An attorney for Maduro told CBS News that he has not been given notice that additional charges could be coming.

item.title: 10/7: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: President Trump returns to Texas to stump for Paxton in San Antonio; new videos show Iranian attacks on U.S. military base in Kuwait.

item.title: Union alleges Bureau of Prisons in contempt for failing to reinstate collective bargaining agreement
item.description: Last week, a judge in Connecticut blocked the Bureau of Prisons from terminating its collective bargaining agreement.
